extracted.intended_audience: priests and bishops of early American Catholic missions (missionary clergy)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical standards for establishing Catholic schools and a quasi-religious community (convent/school) on the frontier, and for conducting missionary instruction and pastoral practice among scattered Catholic populations. Emphasis on educational objectives, community organization, pastoral duties, and devotional practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of Catholic schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Catholic schools are a necessity; building churches alone is not enough to preserve the faith in the hearts of our children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that 'the problem' of falling away from the faith among children is solved by establishing Catholic schools 'where the minds of the young will be guarded against the poisoning influences of an infidel system of education, and imbued with the true spirit of catholic vitality.' It explicitly warns that 'what is to become of our children? Of what use are beautiful churches, if, ten or twenty years hence, they are to be deserted ... liberalized by a system of education that ignores God.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Threefold objects for the proposed 'Friends of Mary' community
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed religious community will have three special objects in view (a threefold institution): rules like the Beguines (leave/return liberty); provide teachers for Catholic schools; help the poor and take care of the sick irrespective of religious belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'The project will have three special objects in view, and will eventually be a threefold institution under the name of Friends of Mary... some kind of rules and obligations like those of the Beguines... The second object will be, to provide from the community teachers for catholic schools; the third, to help the poor and take care of the sick, irrespective of religious belief.' This gives a clear programmatic mission: formation, education, and charitable care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic self-support model for members
rubrics_metrics.description: Members are expected to be able to support themselves by domestic labor (spinning, weaving, sewing) and not necessarily be bound by solemn vows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the proposal: 'They will be able to support themselves by spinning, weaving, and sewing. The Lovers of Mary, as I intend to call them, would not be bound by solemn vows.' This prescribes a modest, self-sustaining economic model suitable for frontier conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and selection of religious women
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer pious, suitably educated young women who desire a more secluded life and are willing to devote themselves to the instruction of Catholic youth (including poor children and slaves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: 'They had found a few pious souls, more favored than others by the grace of God, and sufficiently educated... Twenty young ladies are ready to follow me next Spring... thirteen miles from here.' Also notes that some applicants awaited the success of the undertaking before committing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for capable spiritual leadership and episcopal oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The enterprise should be entrusted to able and worthy superiors and must have a holy director and episcopal approval/oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page recommends: 'its execution and superintendence should be given to the able and worthy-men whom I hoped would soon arrive from Belgium' and expresses anxiety 'about a holy director to be put at the head of the undertaking.' Correspondence with the Vicar-general and Bishop Carroll is shown as essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical building and site requirements for convent/school
rubrics_metrics.description: Convent/school buildings should provide adequate space for living and worship (example given: house seventy feet long with a chapel about as long and wide, out-buildings, and a turret), and be sited near existing mission houses as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit example: 'our convent school-house is under roof; it is seventy feet long, and will have a chapel about as long and wide as the house, surmounted with a turret. Some out-buildings will be added. It is situated one mile from Father Badin's house.' This conveys expectations about scale, components (chapel), and siting on the frontier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence on patronage and land donations
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment depends on donations of land and property from benefactors and on lay generosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete instances: 'James Dent ... offers four hundred acres of land, promising, moreover, to consecrate himself and all he possesses ... the brother ... donates one hundred acres adjoining Father Badin's land.' The guidance indicates securing donors and land is critical to found institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum and instructional aims for children
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should focus on catechism, preparation for first Holy Communion, devotional formation, and molding hearts to Catholic doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: 'After having explained the catechism ... of preparing them for the reception of their first holy communion' and 'he lavished his labors' on children 'molding the hearts of the little ones to the doctrines of the catholic church.' The aim combines doctrinal instruction and sacramental preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child-centered pedagogical methods and devotional practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Use engaging, age-appropriate devices: hymns composed for children, short anecdotes, physical gestures (arms extended in form of a cross, the 'arms up!' practice), rewards (sacred pictures, beads, books), processional and cemetery devotions, and parental involvement.
